settings.heading: Six weeks at a bench in Clerkenwell
settings.text:
Margot Cavelier trained on the benches of Hatton Garden and opened the house in 2016 with one rule that has not changed: nothing is cast speculatively.

A commission begins as a conversation, becomes a drawing, then a wax — and only then metal. You see each stage. Nothing is a surprise except, we hope, the finished thing.

settings.image_alt: A fine gold chain with a single diamond pendant worn at the collarbone
settings.quote: We do not sell what is left over. We make what is asked for.

settings.title: Consultation
settings.text: An hour, in the atelier or by video. We talk about the wearer, the occasion and the budget before anything is drawn.

settings.title: Design
settings.text: Hand drawings first, then a scaled rendering. You see the profile, the gallery and the band width before a stone is bought.

settings.title: Stone selection
settings.text: We source to your brief and show you three or four candidates loose, with certificates, under the same light.

settings.title: Craftsmanship
settings.text: Carved in wax, cast in your metal, then set and finished by hand at the bench. Hallmarked at the London Assay Office.

settings.title: Delivery
settings.text: Collected in the atelier, or delivered insured and signed-for, in a box made for the piece.

settings.heading: Five steps, six to nine weeks
settings.text: The same sequence whether you are remodelling an heirloom or starting from a blank sheet.

settings.image_alt: Raw 18k gold wire, a carved wax ring model and a loose emerald-cut diamond in a paper parcel
settings.heading: Two kinds of diamond, stated plainly
settings.text:
We set natural and lab-grown stones and we will never pretend one is the other. Natural stones are bought through two Antwerp houses we have used since 2017. Lab-grown stones are IGI certified and typically let a client go one to two carats further for the same budget.

Gold is 14k or 18k, recycled where the alloy allows. Every stone above 0.30ct arrives with its own certificate, which is yours to keep.
